heroHeadline: Jersey Nearly Triples Protected Waters to 21.7% as Ocean Conservancy's 2025 Coastal Cleanup Finds Plastic Bottles Still the #1 Beach Pollutant
heroSubtitle: The Government of Jersey announced August 28, 2026 that its Marine Spatial Plan takes effect September 1, expanding waters closed to trawling and dredging from 6.5% to 21.7% of its territorial sea, protecting shallow reefs, maerl beds, seagrass meadows, and kelp forests after three years of consultation with fishing and environmental groups. Separately, Ocean Conservancy released results from its 2025 International Coastal Cleanup on August 26, reporting more than 630,000 volunteers collected roughly 13.9 million pieces of trash worldwide, with plastic beverage bottles (1,338,712 units) and bottle caps (885,854 units) again ranking among the most commonly found items despite being highly recyclable. These developments follow NOAA's July 15 gray whale abundance estimate of ~17,750 individuals, the Australian Institute of Marine Science's August 10 report of coral cover gains on the Great Barrier Reef's Northern and Central sections, and The Ocean Cleanup's August 16 announcement of a 400-meter replacement Interceptor for the Río Ozama in the Dominican Republic.
